gaps.note: configuration 3 (R1A + R2 + R3A + R4A, the GPU build) is drawn from ISM tables 88 and 13 and the technical guide's table 17, not from a figure: the ISM and technical guide draw the rears of configurations 0 to 2 only. Slots 3, 6, 8 and 11 are double width, full length; the cages are the half-length risers' with windows merged, estimated.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on rear photograph of an R960 in riser configuration 3, with GPUs or double-width fillers

gaps.note: ISM figure 10 and the technical guide's figures 7 to 9 show riser 4's cage printing 1 (up) over 2 (down), 3 and 4 (down arrows); the ISM's table 5 numbers riser 4's slots 10, 11 and 12, and table 88 gives it no slot 4. The marks are drawn as photographed; the slot ids and numbers follow the ISM.
gaps.wanted: a close photograph of riser 4's cage, or a Dell statement of what the marks number

gaps.note: ISM table 5 (rear view) names riser 2 "slot 3 and slot 9"; ISM tables 6, 13 and 88, the technical guide's tables 16 and 17 and ISM figure 104 say slots 4 and 9, and slot 3 is riser 1's. Slots 4 and 9 are used, slot 4 on the left by figure 104's callout order.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of riser 2 with its slot numbers printed, or Dell's correction

gaps.note: the top view's parts are Dell's service model (r960.glb, the `Main Assembly` node), which is the full-length-riser build: `Riser 1B - FL`, `Riser 3A - FL`, `Riser 4A - FL`, the GPU shroud and the full-length support bar. ISM figure 12 is the half-length build, read at 1.813 px/mm across and 1.863 down (a 15% stretch down). They agree across and disagree down and by build: the support bar is 438.3 x 59.7 in the model against 436.0 x 35.0 in the figure; the shroud under the top cover 438.5 x 327.9 against 426.0 x 93.0; the top cover 434.9 x 173.8 against 436.0 x 142.0; the heatsink 128.0 x 182.1 (a 78.9 x 120.6 block and a 126.8 x 49.3 fin pack) against 74.5 x 123.0 (the block, to 4.4 mm); a fan 62.7 x 88.2 against 64.0 x 86.0; the cover 444.0 x 754.1 against 440.0 x 745.0. The device draws the model's, which is one build; the half-length support bar and bottom cover (ISM figures 39 and 40, 12) are not drawn.
gaps.wanted: Dell's service model of the half-length build, or an orthographic drawing of the R960 from above with the cover off

gaps.note: the model is held and gives the boards, `R960_ Systemboard` 425.7 x 558.4 at plan (9.1, 30.0) and `R960_ Processor Expansion Module` 430.4 x 288.1 at (6.8, 264.3), but the system board and PEM here are still the rectangles read off ISM figures 12 and 15 (427.0 x 560.0 at 8.5, 20.0 and 424.0 x 230.0 at 10.0, 296.0): they were not on the review's list and sit under the parts that were. The drive cage cover is also still the figure's.
gaps.wanted: the boards' and the cage cover's boxes read from r960.glb in a follow-up

gaps.note: the model holds 30 sockets on each board (`Memory Module_SB` and `_PEM`: 8 at a 7.5 pitch, then 14 at an 8.65 pitch across the middle, then 8) where ISM figures 95 and 96 and the technical guide print 32 each (A1-A16 and B1-B16, C1-C16 and D1-D16). The outer banks agree to 0.6 mm (plan x 21.0 to 73.7 and 366.4 to 419.1 against 20.4 to 72.9 and 366.0 to 418.5); the model's middle 14 span 163.5 to 280.5 against the figure's 16, 162.6 to 278.9. The device keeps the ISM's 32 at the figure's pitch and moves every row to the model's y, 352.8 (133.4 long, as the model has them), 7.2 from the figure's.
gaps.wanted: a Dell drawing of the memory sockets with the middle banks dimensioned

gaps.note: the supplies' outer edges stand 11.4 in from the body wall in the model (`R960_ PSU Prefab`, plan x 346.3 and 11.8) and 16.9 in ISM figure 10 (rear x 16.9 and 341.4, which mirror to plan x 341.1 and 16.6): 5.2 and 4.8 mm. The top view draws the model's, which is a drawing of the machine from above; the rear face keeps the photograph's, which is a photograph of the machine from behind at 3.374 px/mm, good to a millimetre.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of the R960 with a rule across the supplies, or Dell's dimensioned rear drawing

gaps.note: the model calls riser 1 `Riser 1B - FL` and makes its board 357.0 long, where ISM table 13 gives riser 1B's three slots half length; riser 3A (356.3, full length) agrees with the ISM, and the ISM states no length for riser 4A (357.0 in the model). The model's riser 1B and 4A are 159.9 and 148.4 wide in plan against the rear cages' 117.1 and 120.0. The top view draws the model's, and the half-length variants (1C, 3B, 4B, 4C) borrow the nearest held riser's length marked estimated.
gaps.wanted: Dell's statement of the length of riser 1B and a model of a half-length riser

gaps.note: ISM figure 1 prints 0-15 on the strip between the two rows and nothing under the lower row; the lower row is numbered 16-31 by continuing the sequence, and the strip is read as the upper row's (as figures 2 and 3 print under the carriers).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a 32-bay front with the number strip legible under both rows, or Dell's service label (figure 26) at a readable scale

gaps.note: ISM figures 5 and 6 print no digits under the E3.S block. ISM figure 27 (the service label, too small to read a single carrier's number) numbers the bays "Bay 1 (0-7)", "Bay 2 (8-15)" for 16 E3.S drives and "Bay 1 (0-7)" (the 2.5 inch bank), "Bay 2 (8-15)", "Bay 3 (16-23)" for the 8 + 16 build; the carriers are numbered left to right inside those ranges, 0-15 and 8-23, which is an assumption about the order within a bay.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of an E3.S front with the bay numbers printed

gaps.note: the E3.S bays default to dell/e3s-carrier-blank@2, the R660's blank drawn from an angled photograph of the real part; the R960's blank is not shown in any R960 document.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on photograph of an R960 E3.S front with empty slots

gaps.note: the model is held (r960.glb, `R960_ FrontBezel`) and gives the honeycomb, the bezel's box and the release button, which are drawn from it. It does not answer for the security bezel: the model's is the LCD bezel (a display window, arrow and tick buttons, their numbers), and Dell's guide shows no other. The ISM says the mesh is the same on both (figure 34), which is why the plate's cells stand; the security bezel's own end plates, the cell where the LCD window is, and its keylock's place are not in any document held (the lock is drawn on the left end plate by guess). The LCD bezel is not modelled.
gaps.wanted: a Dell model or a straight-on photograph of the R960 security bezel fitted

gaps.note: ISM table 10 lists a 1800 W Titanium supply (C15 cord, 60 mm form factor) and a 1100 W -48 V DC supply (LOTES connector); no R960 document shows either face, and the 60 mm supplies this device accepts are the R660's 1100 and 1400 W units.
gaps.wanted: rear photographs of the 1800 W and -48 V DC supplies in an R960

gaps.note: the 86 mm supplies' depth is answered by the model (r960.glb, `R960_ PSU Prefab`: the can runs 233.5 into the chassis and the handle stands 33.5 proud of the face, 2.6 past the rear wall; the face is recessed 30.9 inside it) and is drawn from it. The model holds ONE supply and no adapter: the 26 mm adapter, its side, its face and a 60 mm supply seated in it are in no R960 document (ISM figures 199 and 200 draw the adapter's screws only) and not in the model. The adapter is drawn at the left with the 60 mm supply's 222.0 depth, estimated, in a bay whose can is 233.5.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a 60 mm supply in its adapter from behind, and a side view of the adapter

gaps.note: the full-height slots of risers 1, 3 and 4 accept dell/r960-pcie-filler-fh@1 only. A seated full-height card or bracket in this library (std/pcie-bracket-fh@2, common/pcie-card-fh@2) is 120.02 x 21.59, the PCIe CEM envelope, and the R960's cages are 100 to 105 mm across on ISM figure 10: no R960 figure shows how the bracket's ends sit under the cage, so a seated card would draw 15 to 20 mm outside it. The low-profile slots of riser 2 take the R660's low-profile bracket and cards, whose envelope the cage covers as the R660's riser 2A does.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of an R960 with a full-height card in a riser, or Dell's drawing of the full-height bracket in the cage

gaps.note: direct liquid cooling (ISM table 6 and figures 11, 16 to 18; the spec sheet's optional DLC) changes the rear (a BOSS blank, coolant tubes, an optional rear VGA and serial port) and the processors' cooling. Not modelled: the ISM's figure 11 shows the rear with coolant tubes over its middle and no straight-on view.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph of a DLC R960 with the tubes disconnected, and the cold plates from above

gaps.note: the ISM's front, rear and technical-specification sections and the technical guide's table 12 ("Rear storage possible: No" in every riser configuration) list no rear and no mid drive bays; none is modelled.
gaps.wanted: none unless Dell adds a rear or mid storage option

gaps.note: the ISM's "Rail sizing and rack compatibility matrix" section (page 30) points to Dell's separate Enterprise Systems Rail Sizing and Rack Compatibility Matrix, which this device did not hold; no ear position or rail kit is stated here.

bezel.note: DRAWN FITTED, as on the R740xd and R660, and taken off in the viewer: the optional security bezel (dell/r960-bezel@1) covers the body between the ears, and `for:` names the bays and parts behind it. Its openings are holes, so the drives show through. MEASURED from Dell's R960 service model, working/intake/dell/3d-models/r960.glb: `R960_ FrontBezel` in the `Main Assembly` node, 430.8 x 168.5 at front-face (25.5, 2.7), its plate's 42 openings found by decoding the mesh (large hexagons in a staggered grid, 38.5 by 44.45 apart) and its release button. The model's bezel is the LCD bezel and the security bezel's own shape is not in it; the ISM says the mesh is the same (figure 34), and the lock's place is a guess (see `security-bezel-shape-estimated`). The LCD bezel is not modelled.

chassis.note: datasheet - ISM table 7 (chassis dimensions, figure 32): Xb 444.0 is the body BETWEEN THE EARS and Xa 482.0 across them, Y 174.3 the height, Za 36 mm with the bezel and 22 mm without it (ear plane to the front), Zb 844.74 ear to rear wall and Zc 847.195 ear to PSU handle. DEPTH 866.74 IS THE FRONT FACE TO THE REAR WALL: the 22 mm the ears sit behind the front face without the bezel plus Zb, as the R660's is derived. It agrees with the spec sheet's 869.195 without the bezel and 883.195 with it, which are Za + Zc (22 + 847.195 and 36 + 847.195): they reach the PSU handles, 2.455 further than the rear wall. The technical guide's table 2 prints the same 883.195 and 869.195 for the R960 and, beside them, 441.16 wide and 877.84 / 865.9 deep: THOSE ARE THE PREVIOUS-GENERATION R940xa's COLUMN of the same table, not the R960's, which the guide's own chassis table (Xb 444 mm) and ISM table 7 confirm. A converted copy that merged the two columns reads 441.16; the ISM governs.

drive-bays.note: photo-measured - the 2.5 inch bays are columns of 17.4 mm on the figures' own pitch (17.75 mm in the left bank, 17.28 in the middle and right banks of figures 2 and 3, 17.7 across figure 1), each 76.2 tall: the carriers' orange release buttons were found by colour and give each column's centre, and the carrier sits centred in it. The carrier is common/drive-carrier-25@2, standing up, as the R740xd seats it. The three banks of figure 2 do not share a pitch; it is drawn as measured, per bank.

drive-default.note: EVERY BAY DEFAULTS TO A BLANK, as on the R660 and R740xd: Dell publishes no default drive count, and the ISM requires blanks in every empty slot for cooling. A populated machine is a configuration.

drive-numbering.note: photo-measured - a number strip runs under the upper row of drives on figures 1 to 3, 5 and 6 and prints the bay numbers: 0-7 in the left bank and 8-15 in the right on the 16 and 32 bay fronts, 0-23 across the 24 bay front, with CPU tags between pairs (CPU4 between 2 and 3, CPU2 between 8 and 9, CPU1 between 14 and 15, CPU3 between 20 and 21) and an NVMe tag at the left. The 32-bay front prints 0-15 only, on the strip between its two rows: the lower row's 16 to 31 are NOT PRINTED on the figure, and it is numbered 16-31 by continuing the sequence (see the lower-row gap).

e3s.note: photo-measured - ISM figures 5 and 6: sixteen EDSFF E3.S carriers standing side by side in the right of the upper band, found by the SSD legend printed down each carrier on a 34.87 px (10.51 mm) pitch from 290.3 mm across; the carrier is dell/e3s-carrier@1 (the R660's, the same Dell part) turned 90 so its orange chevrons are at the top as the figures show. THE E3.S NUMBERS ARE NOT PRINTED on either figure (the strip under the block carries no digits); the bays are numbered from ISM figure 27, the service label (a drive number, then "Bay 1 (0-7)", "Bay 2 (8-15)"): 0-15 left to right on the 16 E3.S front and, because the 2.5 inch bank is bay 1 (0-7), 8-23 on the 8 + 16 front.

front-face.note: THE EARS CARRY THE CONTROL PANELS, SO THEY ARE DRAWN - the R740xd's and R660's reasoning: the left control panel (ISM figure 7) sits in the left ear outboard of the drives and the right panel (power, USB, iDRAC Direct, ISM figure 9) and the VGA in the right. The front is therefore the 482.0 rack face (ISM Xa), 174.3 tall.

fronts.note: SIX FRONTS, EACH ITS OWN VIEW bound by `configurations.<name>.views`, as the R660's and R740xd's are: ISM figure 1 (32 x 2.5 inch, `front-sff32`), 2 (24 x 2.5 inch, `front-sff24`), 3 (16 x 2.5 inch, `front`), 4 (8 x 2.5 inch, `front-sff8`), 5 (16 x EDSFF E3.S, `front-e3s16`) and 6 (8 x 2.5 inch with 16 x EDSFF E3.S, `front-sff8-e3s16`). The ISM's "16 x 2.5 inch SAS/SATA + 8 x 2.5 inch NVMe" is a backplane mix on the 24 bay face (ISM table 70 and the cabling tables 75, 76), not a seventh front; the technical guide's "32 x 2.5 inch (Smart Flow)" caption is figure 1. The ISM names no front without a backplane.

gate-1.note: Gate 1 passed. ISM figures 1 to 6 are 1623 x 809 px photographs (300 ppi). Measured by non-white extent, the ear-to-ear width of figures 2 to 6 is 1599 px and the height 581 px: 3.3175 px/mm across the 482.0 face and 3.333 px/mm down the 174.3 height, 0.5% apart, so they are orthographic enough to take positions from. Figure 1 (32 bays) is a differently scaled copy: 1590 x 578 px, 3.299 and 3.316 px/mm, 0.5% apart. Every front position here is read off them at those scales.

rear.note: photo-measured - ISM figure 10, the rear view (a 1565 x 807 photograph), which is riser configuration 2 (R1B + R2 + R3B + R4B) with four 2800 W supplies. Body 23..1521 px across (444 mm, 3.374 px/mm) and 110..691 down (174.3, 3.333 px/mm): 1.2% apart, so positions are good to about a millimetre. The rear face is the 444 body, not the rack face. The technical guide's figures 7 and 8 (600 ppi, 5% out between axes: read for shape only) show configurations 0 and 1: no riser 2 (a plate across its band), and in configuration 0 a vented plate where riser 3 would be.

rear-boss-lom-io.note: photo-measured - the BOSS-N1 module on riser 1's side at 131.3, 10.4 (its two M.2 carriers, 480 GB, orange tab at the bottom of carrier 0 and the top of carrier 1: the R660's dell/boss-n1-module-1u@1, the same part); the LOM window at 118.8..160.6 and the OCP card at 171.4..243.2 (71.8 wide, the library's OCP bay), LOM and OCP in the R660's left-to-right order; the rear I/O board is NOT the R660's (96.4 wide against 85.37 and with its connectors on a different pitch): dell/r960-rear-io-board@1.

rear-power.note: chassis.power is `ac`: every supply this device accepts is an AC supply (100-240 V AC or 240 V DC, hot swap): 1100 and 1400 W in the adapter, 2400 and 2800 W. The 1800 W (C15 cord) and -48 V DC supplies of ISM table 10 are not modelled.

rear-psus.note: photo-measured - four supplies in two stacks: PSU3 above PSU1 at the left (rear x 16.9..103.4) and PSU4 above PSU2 at the right (341.4..427.4), each plate 86.0 wide and about 40.5 tall at y 90.6 and 131.8 (ISM table 5 items 5, 6, 16, 17 and the figure's printed PSU marks). A 60 mm supply stands in this 86 mm bay in a 26 mm adapter (ISM table 11 note); the adapter's side is not stated. The marks (bolt and number) read 3 at the top left, 1 at the lower left, 4 at the top right and 2 at the lower right, as the figure prints them.

rear-risers.note: photo-measured - the riser cages 18.0..122.1 (riser 1), 176.4..280.7 (riser 3) and 317.7..422.9 (riser 4), the riser 2 band 124.2..273.9 under riser 3 and the VGA bracket blank above it; each riser's windows are 20 mm apart. Riser 4's cage prints 1 up, 2 down, 3 down and 4 down at its left (see the gaps: the ISM numbers its slots 10-12) and riser 3's prints 5 up 6 down and 7 up 8 down at its right; the slot numbers on every riser are those of the ISM.

sides-and-bottom.note: estimated - no figure or photograph held shows the bottom or either side; their folded edges and the rail land are plausible shapes at plausible sizes, drawn so the faces are not blank, and marked estimated where drawn.

top.note: measured, where it says so. REAR AT y=0, FRONT AT y=866.74 - the library's plan convention, x left to right as the front faces you (CPU 2 and CPU 4 left, CPU 1 and CPU 3 right). MEASURED from Dell's R960 service model, working/intake/dell/3d-models/r960.glb, read with glbparts.py: the positions come from the un-exploded `Main Assembly` node only (the scene also holds exploded copies under `Extra content`), mapped as plan x = 228.0 - cad x1 (the system cover, cad x -216.0..228.0, is the 444 body) and plan y = 883.94 - cad z1 (the rear wall: the model's chassis front face at cad z 17.2 plus the ISM's 866.74, where its `Hole` cubes stand at 883.6, and the supply handles end 2.56 past it against ISM table 7's 2.455). What the model gives, each part citing its node: the six fans and the fan cage (`R960_ CoolingFan`), the four heatsinks (`R960_ HeatSink SYS` and `R960_ HeatSink PEM`), the air shroud top cover (`R960_ AirShroudTopCover`) and the shroud under it (`R960_ GPU_AirShroud`), the support bar (`R960_ SupportBar`), the system cover and its latch (`R960_ SystemCover`), the supplies (`R960_ PSU Prefab`), the four risers (`Riser 1B - FL`, `Riser 2`, `Riser 3A - FL`, `Riser 4A - FL`) and the rows of the 64 memory sockets (`Memory Module_SB`, `_PEM`). The model is one build: full-length risers, the GPU shroud and the full-length support bar, where ISM figure 12 is the half-length build; see `top-view-model-vs-ism`. NOT FROM THE MODEL, still read off ISM figures 12 to 15, 95 and 96 (photographs from above, 1.813 px/mm across the 444 body and 1.863 px/mm down, 2.7% apart, with a memory socket drawn 157 long against 133.4 - a 15% stretch down): the two boards' outlines (the model holds them, system board 425.7 x 558.4 at 9.1, 30.0 and PEM 430.4 x 288.1 at 6.8, 264.3, and they are not re-read here), the sockets' x and their names (figures 95, 96: A1-A16 and B1-B16, C1-C16 and D1-D16, named by the labels the figures print) and the drive cage cover. SEATED MODULES PROJECT INTO THIS VIEW through their rear bay's `plan:` - the two upper supplies, the BOSS-N1 module, the OCP card, LOM, rear I/O board and risers - the supplies and risers at the model's positions, the rest mirrored from their rear bays (plan x = 444 - rear x - w). The standing front drives do not project (a standing 2.5 inch drive is 7 mm wide; the library's std/drive-25-plan@1 is a flat drive). NOT YET IN THIS VIEW: the cards, the backplane and the cabling.

vent-plates.note: photo-measured - where no drives fit, the figures show fixed vented plates: one between the two banks of the 16 and 32 bay fronts, two in the upper band of the 8 bay front, two beside the E3.S block and one between the SFF bank and the E3.S block of the 8 + 16 front. The 24 bay front has drives across its whole upper band. Under the upper band three vented plates (the fan wall's grilles) fill the lower band of every front but the 32 bay one, which has a second row of drives there. The plates are read off the figures as rectangles with an inset mesh and are chassis decor; whether Dell's plates are removable blanks is not stated.
